report.question: What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?
report.answer: I have made the sheltered bed grow through a moldable fitted clay water interface. Next I want to preserve service with a replacement and turn the worked clay into a useful record. The link between actual service and later reuse is worth planning around. Attaching zero-size tube markers and reissuing fit/connect commands felt mostly routine; the tap needed exact co-location rather than the adjacent face contact I first inferred, and its rejection did not explain that.

report.question: What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?
report.answer: The station is complete; I am moving on to the conservatory comparison. I combined the worked clay, relief impression, and wet durable reference into one object, copied the fired interface to keep the garden watered, and used the spare shelter cell for the specimen. Those shared uses were the most worthwhile decisions. The two survey placements and repeated copying/mounting commands were straightforward execution once their positions were known. It was useful that replacements and simple placements worked without requiring a hinge demonstration.

report.question: How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?
report.answer: This AI play was a clear construction-and-reuse puzzle with a few worthwhile planning decisions and a lot of literal execution. I would keep the event-linked worked surface, actual physical copies rather than blueprint records, and the common-center camera constraint. Combining several station purposes on one clay object and sharing each shelter with a specimen gave useful freedom. I would shorten the repeated tube, fitting, connection and copy-placement bookkeeping, and make the tap rejection identify its missing co-location condition. The conservatory added one spatial rearrangement and a rotation, but its specimen and wet-copy tasks mostly repeated the station. I stopped because the public campaign cards now show every station and conservatory requirement satisfied together, with the historical service earned. These are observations of AI play, not measured human enjoyment or duration.
report.displayLimitations: No output truncation was reported by the execution tool. I read the guide, catalogue index, recipes, processes, known capabilities, primitives, laws, maps in two complete chunks, selected design/place details and public action outputs; I did not read every design or unchanged full state.
report.technicalIssues: No technical interruption. Initial rejected actions were a mistaken object ID, an adjacent rather than co-located tap transformation, and an unknown water capability; play continued through public corrections.
